title.justification: The title is clearly stated at the beginning of the paper.

analysis.description: This paper introduces 'fairwashing', which involves promoting the false perception that a machine learning model respects ethical values, even if it doesn't. The paper presents a technique called LaundryML, which uses a regularized rule list enumeration algorithm to approximate unfair black-box models with fairer ones while maintaining high fidelity to the original model.

type.justification: The paper involves empirical evaluation through experiments on real-world datasets to demonstrate the possibility of fairwashing by using rationalization techniques with machine learning models.
type.quote: We empirically evaluate our rationalization technique on black-box models trained on real-world datasets and show that one can obtain rule lists with high fidelity to the black-box model while being considerably less unfair at the same time.

name.justification: The paper is focused on machine learning models and the risk of misusing model explanations to present them as fair when they are not.
name.quote: Black-box explanation is the problem of explaining how a machine learning model – whose internal logic is hidden to the auditor and generally complex – produces its outcomes.

name.justification: The paper focuses primarily on the fairness of machine learning models and the potential for performing fairwashing.
name.quote: ...raising the awareness of this issue, which we believe to be a serious concern related to the use of black-box explanation...

name.justification: The paper deals with the interpretability of machine learning models, specifically through an explanation of black-box models.
name.quote: Examples of such interfaces include linear models (Ribeiro et al., 2016), decision trees (Breiman, 2017), rule lists (Rivest, 1987; Letham et al., 2015; Angelino et al., 2018) and rule sets (Li et al., 2002).

name.justification: The paper references CORELS as a supervised machine learning algorithm used as part of the LaundryML algorithm for rule list enumeration.
name.quote: CORELS (Angelino et al., 2018) is a supervised machine learning algorithm which takes as input a training set with n predictor variables, all assumed to be binary.

is_contributed.justification: CORELS itself is not contributed by this paper but is used within the proposed LaundryML algorithm.
is_contributed.quote: CORELS (Angelino et al., 2018) is a supervised machine learning algorithm...

is_executed.justification: CORELS is discussed in the context of the algorithm but there is no specific mention of execution hardware like GPU or CPU for this model within the text.
is_executed.quote: CORELS (Angelino et al., 2018) is a supervised machine learning algorithm...

is_compared.justification: The paper does not provide numerical comparisons of CORELS with other models; it is described as part of the methodology.
is_compared.quote: CORELS selects the rule list that minimizes the objective function.
